chapters.title: Algorithms and Problem Solving
chapters.main_concept: Explains what computational problems are and how to classify them, the role of algorithms, solvability and complexity (P, NP, NP-hard, NP-complete), Big-O analysis of time and space, design techniques (divide and conquer, greedy, dynamic programming, backtracking) and common sorting, searching and graph traversal algorithms.
formulas: Big O classes: O(1) constant, O(n) linear, O(n^2) quadratic, O(log n) logarithmic
Pairwise comparisons approx n(n-1) (quadratic growth)
Merge Sort / Quick Sort: O(n log n)
Bubble Sort: O(n^2); Selection Sort: O(n^2)
Binary Search: O(log n) (sorted list only)
BFS and DFS: O(V + E)
Process: Generate-and-Test (generator -> tester -> correct? stop : regenerate)
Process: Bubble sort, selection sort, linear search, binary search, BFS (enqueue/dequeue), DFS (push/pop) step lists

chapters.title: Data Analytics
chapters.main_concept: Covers descriptive statistics (central tendency, dispersion, probability), data collection and preparation, building and evaluating simple statistical models (linear/logistic regression, k-means clustering) with ethics, and data visualisation types and tools (Excel/Google Sheets).

subtopics.title: Using Excel and Google Sheets for Visualization
Creating and Interpreting Visualizations (printed as 5.2.2; should be 5.5.2)

formulas: Mean = sum of values / number of values (e.g. (50+60+70+80+90)/5 = 70)
Median = middle value (even n: average of two middle values, e.g. (60+70)/2 = 65)
Mode = most frequent value (can be multimodal)
Variance sigma^2 = Sum(x_i - mu)^2 / N (Class A = 12.56, Class B = 454)
Standard deviation sigma = sqrt( Sum(x_i - mu)^2 / N ) (Class A ~ 3.55, Class B ~ 21.26)
Probability = favourable outcomes / total outcomes (coin heads = 1/2)
Simple linear regression: Y = beta0 + beta1*X + epsilon
Worked model: Earnings = 100 + 40 x Customers (slope 200/5 = 40; intercept 500 - 40x10 = 100)
Prediction error = predicted - actual (1,220 - 1,250 = -30 Rs)
Process: model development - define problem, collect data, choose algorithm, train, evaluate
Process: chart in Excel/Sheets - enter data, select, choose chart type, customise, interpret
